# ND-100 mapping PROM (decode PLA)

<!-- generated by src/eng/nd100-mapping-table.py from the chip dumps in REFERENCE/DECODE; do not edit by hand -->

What the three 82S185 PROMs in slots b18, b19 and b20 of the ND-100 CPU card hold, how the hardware uses them, and how this was checked.

## How the hardware uses it

**Facts read from the files** (the manual text is in `ND100-MICROCODE_combined.md`, bit 27 and bits 0-11 of the microword; the rest from the chip dumps and the assembled sources):

1. The microcode does a *mapped jump* when a microinstruction has `T,MAPJ` and the next microinstruction is a jump (`T,JMP`). The jump address is then not taken from bits 0-11 of that microword (they must be 0) but from the mapping PROM. The interrupt hardware can replace it with an interrupt vector, unless `COMM,CLIRQ` was given. The label `FETCH` (0o16, banner `MAPPING POINT FOR ALL INSTRUCTIONS`) is the place where this happens for every machine instruction.

2. The PROM is 2048 words of 12 bits (three 82S185, each 2K x 4). Chip b20 holds bits 3-0 of the entry, b19 bits 7-4, b18 bits 11-8. The entry is a microcode address (12 bits, the same width as the branch address of the microword). This reading puts 2022 of the 3033S entries exactly on a label of the assembled source; the other five chip orders and the inverted forms give at most 1136.

3. The address of the PROM is **IR bits 15-6** (10 lines: opcode, addressing mode bits and the top two displacement bits of the machine instruction in the instruction register) plus **one more line** (index bit 10, value 0o2000). Evidence for the 10 bits: every memory reference opcode owns a run of exactly 32 entries (`STZ` 0o0000-0o0037, `STA` 0o0040-0o0077, `STT`, `STX`, `STD`, `LDD`, `STF`, `LDF`, `MIN`, `LDA`, ..., 32 x opcode number), and the manual names `1403xx` as `CUST2`, which is index 0o1403. The low 6 bits of the instruction are not used by the PROM: the microcode decodes them itself with the vectored jumps (`T,JMP0-3`, `T,JMP8-10`, `T,JMPALD`, `T,JMPAOPR`, `A,REG`).

4. The two halves of the PROM (index bit 10 = 0 and = 1) are equal except for 84 of 1024 entries. In every one of them the lower half (bit 10 = 0) has the entry of the label `PRIVI` and the upper half (bit 10 = 1) the real routine (`IDENT`, `LDWCS`, `TRA`, `TRR`, `MCL`, `MST`, `PIONF`, `WAIT`, `SRB`, `LRB`, `IRW`, `IRR`, `IOX`, `SINTR`) or `ILLIN` for opcodes that do not exist. So index bit 10 is a *privileged instructions allowed* line: 0 gives the privileged instruction trap, 1 lets the instruction run.

**Inferred, not proved by the files** (the schematics of the 3033 card would settle it): which signal drives index bit 10. The manual has `COND,RESTR` ("restricted mode, true if ring 0-1"); the behaviour above fits the line being *not restricted* (ring 2-3). Also not explained by the files: customer instruction entries (index 0o1402-0o1427 for opcodes 1402xx-1427xx) hold 0o7400-0o7413 on the 3033S, but the manual says execution goes to the writable control store at 0o4001-0o4015 after `LWCS` (`1403xx` = `CUST2` = 0o4001, and the PROM holds 0o7401). The difference is the bits 0o3400 of the 12 bit address; the logic that turns one into the other (the ROM-out-of-range test of the manual) is not in our files.

**To build an ND-100 microcode CPU from this** (what a model needs):

```
at the microinstruction with T,MAPJ followed by T,JMP:
    index   = (IR >> 6) & 0x3FF                 ; IR bits 15-6
    if not restricted_mode: index |= 0x400      ; index bit 10 (inferred line, see above)
    next_uaddr = MAP[index]                     ; 12 bit entry from the 2048 word table below
unless an interrupt is pending and COMM,CLIRQ was not given: then the interrupt hardware supplies the address
```

The table can be rebuilt from the six chip files in `REFERENCE/DECODE/`; the runs below are the same data in readable form.

## Checks

- **3033S**: 2022 of 2048 entries are the address of a label of the assembled source. The other 26 entries (addresses 0o7377 0o7400 0o7401 0o7402 0o7403 0o7404 0o7405 0o7406 0o7407 0o7410 0o7411 0o7412 0o7413) are in the writable control store range, where the printed ROM listing has no code (the customer instruction entries 0o7400-0o7413 and, on the 3033S, 0o7377 for index 0o1431, which the 3033E-CX maps to `MOVEW`).
- **3033E-CX**: 2028 of 2048 entries are the address of a label of the assembled source. The other 20 entries (addresses 0o7400 0o7402 0o7403 0o7404 0o7405 0o7406 0o7407 0o7410 0o7411 0o7412) are in the writable control store range, where the printed ROM listing has no code (the customer instruction entries 0o7400-0o7413 and, on the 3033S, 0o7377 for index 0o1431, which the 3033E-CX maps to `MOVEW`).
- **ND-110 cross check**: the ND-110 microcode (`ND-110-RASK.uc`) has the first microinstruction of each machine instruction at `0o6000 + index`, with the instruction names as labels (`STZ` at 0o6000, `STA` at 0o6040, `FAD` at 0o7000, `JUMP` at 0o7240 ...). The same index in the 3033S PROM (bit 10 = 1) points at a label of the same name in 68 cases and at a spelling variant or another name in 15 cases. The variants are the same instruction (ND-110 / ND-100 label): 1240 JUMP/JMP, 1401 COMM/COMME, 1435 WCS/LDWCS, 1440 SWAP/SWAP0, 1444 RAND/RAND0, 1450 REXO/REXO0, 1454 RORA/RORA0, 1460 RADD/RADD0, 1500 TRA4/TRA, 1501 TRR4/TRR, 1534 IRWX/IRW, 1536 IRRX/IRR, 1600 IOT/ILLIN, 1740 BSET/BSET0, 1750 BSKP/BSKP0. The ND-110 table also shows that the index is IR bits 15-6 (`IR >> 6`), not `IR >> 3`: the manual gives `LWCS` as 143500 and `CUST2` as 1403xx, and the ND-110 has the labels `WCS` at 0o6000 + 0o1435 and `S3SEG` at 0o6000 + 0o1403 (the 3033E-CX card maps 1403xx to `S3SEG`), while `143500 >> 3` would be 0o14350 and has no entry in the table.
- **3033S against 3033E-CX**: 8 of 2048 entries differ. The 3033E-CX card maps `COMME` (index 0o1401), `S3SEG` (0o1403), `GECO` (0o1427) and `MOVEW` (0o1431) to routines in its extension bank (0o4037, 0o6350, 0o6325, 0o6477) where the 3033S card has the `PRIVI` trap or a writable control store address. The ND-110 table has the same four names at the same indices (`COMM`, `S3SEG`, `GECO`, `MOVEW`).
